newsitem.title: UK: Bulgarian Brady prices fall on demonstrations.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Brady prices fall on demonstrations.

text.p: Bulgarian Brady bond prices fell about a point on Monday as traders were rattled by the growing politicial unrest which they fear could mean yet more delays to economic reform.
Interest arrears bonds (IABs) were quoted in morning trading at 48-5/8 cents in the dollar, a drop of a cent from last Friday's close.

Protests against the ruling party, spurred by Bulgaria's economic crisis, are intensifying and trade unions are now planning one-hour warning strikes to press opposition demands for an early general election.
"If there are elections now, it delays the whole process," one U.S. bank trader said.
"What the market wants to see is a currency board and payment on their Bradys. If there is any delay to those, prices will fall," he said.
The currency board is crucial to winning a loan from the Intenrational Monetary Board without which analysts expect Bulgaria will be forced to default.
The government earlier pledged that it would honour Brady bond coupon payments of $135 million later this month.
